blocks.text: The Concern Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA) had for Matters they were Unaware of

Hadhrat Muhammad bin Seereen says, "After Rasulullaah ﷺ there was none more concerned about not knowing something than Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and after Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) there was none more concerned about not knowing something than Hadhrat Umar (RA). When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) needed to pass a verdict and could not find a verse of the Qur'aan or a narration of Rasulullaah ﷺ that applied directly to the situation, he would say, 'I shall now practise Ijtihaad. Should it be correct, it is from Allaah and if it is wrong, it is my error and I seek Allaah's forgiveness for it." [^2]
Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s Letter to Hadhrat Shurayh in this Regard

Hadhrat Shurayh narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once wrote to him saying, "When a matter presents itself before you, pass your verdict according to the Book of Allaah. If the matter is not mentioned in the Book of Allaah, pass your verdict according to what Rasulullaah ﷺ directed. If such a matter presents itself that is neither in the Book of Allaah, about which Rasulullaah ﷺ has issued no directives, then pass your verdict by that about which the Ulema are unanimous. However, if such a matter presents itself that is neither in the Book of Allaah, about which Rasulullaah ﷺ has issued no directives and about which no scholar has commented, then you have one of two choices. If you prefer to practise Ijtihaad, you may proceed. Otherwise, if you prefer, you may desist from doing so. In my opinion, desisting is the best course for you." [^3]
The Statement of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) Concerning Ijtihaad

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "When any of you has to pass a verdict, he should pass his verdict according to the Book of Allaah. If the matter is not mentioned in the Book of Allaah, he should pass his verdict as Rasulullaah ﷺ had done. If such a matter presents itself that is neither in the Book of Allaah, about which Rasulullaah ﷺ has not passed a verdict, then he should pass his verdict as the righteous scholars had done. However, if such a matter presents itself that is neither in the Book of Allaah and about which neither Rasulullaah ﷺ nor the righteous scholars have passed verdicts, he should practise Ijtihaad. He must then be firm on his verdict without being embarrassed about it." Another narration adds that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "He should then practise Ijtihaad and (when stating his verdict, he must)
